headline: Park Pass Requirements and Lake Access Shuttles
reservation: A Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily entry fee is mandatory for all visitors entering the park. Due to extreme demand, parking at Lake Louise and Moraine Lake is highly restricted; Moraine Lake Road is closed to private vehicles, requiring shuttle or transit reservations. Always confirm the current booking window on the Parks Canada site.

days.title: Alpine Lakes and High Peaks

stops.name: Lake Louise
stops.detail: View the turquoise waters and Victoria Glacier, then walk the shoreline trail toward the back of the lake.

stops.name: Moraine Lake
stops.detail: Accessible via shuttle, this lake in the Valley of the Ten Peaks offers the famous Rockpile viewpoint.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the drive to the shuttle hub, plus shuttle transit time; conditions vary.
days.note: Shuttle reservations are essential and often sell out months in advance; check for last-minute releases.

days.title: Bow Valley and Heritage Hot Springs

stops.name: Johnston Canyon
stops.detail: Walk the catwalks built into the limestone canyon walls to view the Lower and Upper Falls.

stops.name: Cave and Basin National Historic Site
stops.detail: Learn about the birthplace of Canada's national parks at these thermal springs and historic bathhouses.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes to 1 hour between Canmore and Johnston Canyon via the Bow Valley Parkway; conditions vary.
days.note: Sections of the Bow Valley Parkway may have seasonal vehicle restrictions to protect wildlife; check local signs.

days.title: Panoramic Summits and Icefield Views
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from Lake Louise Village

stops.name: Bow Lake
stops.detail: A stop along the Icefields Parkway providing views of the Crowfoot Glacier and Wapta Icefield.

stops.name: Peyto Lake
stops.detail: Take the short walk to the Bow Summit viewpoint for a look at the wolf-shaped glacial lake.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours for a return trip on the Icefields Parkway; conditions vary.
days.note: Fuel is extremely limited on the Icefields Parkway; ensure your tank is full before leaving Lake Louise.

intel.title: Banff Townsite Parking
intel.text: The town of Banff utilizes intercept lots and paid parking zones. Use the free shuttle from the train station lot to minimize congestion in the town center.

intel.title: Parkway Connectivity
intel.text: Cell service is reliable in Banff and Lake Louise but disappears entirely on long stretches of the Icefields Parkway. Download maps and emergency info before heading north.

intel.title: Regional Stations
intel.text: Fuel is available in Canmore, Banff, and Lake Louise Village. The only station on the Icefields Parkway is at Saskatchewan River Crossing, which is seasonal.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Access
intel.text: Moraine Lake Road typically opens in late May and closes after the first week of October. Winter visitors must use specialized transport for certain valley areas.

intel.title: Wildlife Corridors
intel.text: Speed limits are strictly enforced to protect wildlife; certain areas may have 'no stopping' zones if bears or goats are present near the roadway.

plan.arrival: Collect your vehicle at Calgary International and drive west on Highway 1. Canmore is an ideal base for groceries and supplies before entering the park gates.
plan.vehicle: Winter tires or snow chains are legally required on most park roads from November to April; check rental agreements for mountain specifications.
plan.goldenHour: Vermilion Lakes offers a classic view of Mount Rundle for sunset, with colors changing based on seasonal clouds.
